infrastructure: Docker container on AWS App Runner with RDS MySQL

pathways.name: Move to Cloud Native

findings.description: Single-file monolith (3,193 lines) with all domains tightly coupled — orders, inventory, payments, shipping, returns, customer service, and UI in one file
No separation of concerns — business logic, data access, routing, and presentation all interleaved
Synchronous request processing with no event-driven patterns
Hardcoded business configuration (warehouse coordinates, carrier rates, tax rates) embedded in source code
Database schema initialization and seeding at application startup creates coupling to the deployment lifecycle
No API versioning or contract separation — internal and external consumers share the same endpoints
Session/state managed implicitly via database queries with no caching layer

recommended_actions: Decompose into bounded contexts: Order Management, Inventory, Payments, Shipping, Returns, Customer Service
Introduce an API gateway pattern to manage routing and cross-cutting concerns
Externalize configuration using AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store or AWS AppConfig
Adopt event-driven communication (Amazon EventBridge or Amazon SQS) between domains

pathways.name: Move to Containers

findings.description: Working Dockerfile with PHP 8.2-apache base, non-root user, and healthcheck already exists
docker-compose.yml provides local orchestration with health checks and security options (read-only filesystem, no-new-privileges)
No multi-stage build — image includes build tools (apt packages) in the runtime layer
Single container runs entire application — no opportunity for independent scaling of domains
No container orchestration beyond App Runner — no Kubernetes manifests, ECS task definitions, or service mesh
Container image not optimized for size — uses full apache base rather than lightweight alternatives

recommended_actions: Implement multi-stage Docker build to reduce image size and attack surface
After decomposition, create individual container images per service for independent scaling
Consider Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate for container orchestration if more control than App Runner is needed
Implement container image scanning in the build pipeline

pathways.name: Move to Open Source

findings.description: Entire stack is open source: PHP 8.2, Apache HTTP Server, MySQL 8.0
No proprietary runtime dependencies or vendor lock-in on application tier
No dependency management tool (Composer) — all code is hand-written with no third-party packages
No framework adoption — vanilla PHP limits productivity and community ecosystem leverage

recommended_actions: Adopt a modern PHP framework (Laravel, Symfony) or consider migration to a more cloud-native language/framework
Introduce Composer for dependency management to leverage community packages

pathways.name: Move to Managed Databases

findings.description: CloudFormation IaC already provisions Amazon RDS MySQL with Multi-AZ, encryption, automated backups, and enhanced monitoring
IAM database authentication enabled in the IaC template
Single shared database with 9 tables serving all domains — no domain-level data isolation
Application uses direct SQL with no ORM or abstraction layer — schema changes require code changes throughout
No read replicas configured for read-heavy workloads (product catalog queries)
No database migration tooling — schema created imperatively at app startup
Hardcoded fallback credentials in application code

recommended_actions: Implement database-per-service pattern after decomposition
Introduce a migration tool (Flyway, Liquibase, or Phinx) for schema management
Add read replicas for the product catalog domain
Remove hardcoded fallback credentials; use AWS Secrets Manager
Consider Amazon Aurora MySQL for improved performance and availability

pathways.name: Move to Managed Analytics

findings.description: No analytics or reporting infrastructure — all data access is direct SQL against the operational database
No data pipeline for ETL/ELT of transactional data into analytics-optimized stores
Business metrics (order counts, revenue, inventory levels) computed on-demand via application queries
No event streaming or change data capture for real-time analytics
Customer interaction data and order history stored in operational tables with no archival strategy

recommended_actions: Implement change data capture (CDC) from RDS using AWS DMS
Adopt Amazon Redshift or Amazon Athena for analytical queries
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for real-time event streaming
Build dashboards with Amazon QuickSight

pathways.name: Move to Modern DevOps

findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline — deployment is manual via deploy.sh (docker-compose build/up)
No automated testing whatsoever — no unit tests, integration tests, or end-to-end tests
No code quality tooling (linters, static analysis, security scanning)
CloudFormation IaC exists for production infrastructure but has no pipeline to deploy it
No environment promotion strategy (dev → staging → production)
No structured logging or observability integration — errors logged to Apache error log only
ECR image scanning configured but no pipeline to act on scan results
No rollback strategy — deployment is fire-and-forget

recommended_actions: Implement CI/CD pipeline using AWS CodePipeline + CodeBuild or GitHub Actions
Add automated testing: start with API integration tests, then unit tests
Introduce PHP static analysis (PHPStan, Psalm) and linting in CI pipeline
Implement structured logging with correlation IDs; ship to CloudWatch
Add application performance monitoring with AWS X-Ray
Implement blue/green or canary deployment strategy

pathways.name: Move to AI

findings.description: No AI/ML integration — product recommendations, search, and pricing are all static or rule-based
No data pipeline to support ML model training (customer behavior, purchase patterns)
Customer sentiment field exists in interactions table but is never populated by automated analysis
No chatbot or AI-assisted customer service capabilities
No personalization engine for product discovery or marketing

recommended_actions: Implement product recommendations using Amazon Personalize
Add natural language search with Amazon Kendra or OpenSearch semantic capabilities
Use Amazon Comprehend for automated sentiment analysis
Integrate Amazon Bedrock for AI-powered customer service chatbot
Build ML pipelines with Amazon SageMaker for demand forecasting
